Underbody impact resistance of an EV battery pack

Mar 2025 — Sep 2025

MSc dissertation — Oxford Brookes University

  • Created 21700 cylindrical-cell, blade-prismatic-cell and aluminium pack-casing CAD/FE models in SolidWorks and HyperMesh, with LS-DYNA explicit impact analysis and mesh-convergence studies.
  • Compared cell force–displacement and pack response against published physical-test and validated-model data; noted the cylindrical-cell model had a larger validation error than the prismatic-cell and casing models.
  • Ran a mass–velocity parametric sweep and compared both pack architectures at a 3 kg, 30 m/s (1,350 J) underbody strike. In the model, the prismatic layout reduced jellyroll deformation by about 70% and casing deformation by about 50% relative to the cylindrical layout.
  • Evaluated topography optimisation, PMI foam, Navtruss and carbon-fibre composite cover absorbers. The 6.9 kg carbon-fibre cover absorbed about 30% of initial impact energy and reduced peak casing stress to 198 MPa and cell-body deformation from 15 mm to 9 mm.
  • Checked energy balance and hourglass energy, and identified the need for assembly-level and coupled thermal/electrical validation before linking deformation directly to cell shorting.

Composite hydrogen chassis: design, structural analysis and NCAP-inspired impact simulation

Jan 2025 — May 2025

Postgraduate group project and impact modelling report — Oxford Brookes University

  • Co-designed a 2.10 × 1.41 × 0.25 m composite envelope packaging two hydrogen cylinders, a fuel cell and a battery, with a removable lid and reinforced mounting points for service access.
  • Set the laminate design against project targets of at least 10,000 N/mm bending rigidity, 45,000 Nm/degree torsional rigidity and under 110 kg for the chassis and hydrogen tanks; used classical laminate theory and Tsai-Hill checks alongside HyperMesh/OptiStruct static analysis.
  • Compared low-volume M60J/T800 and higher-volume T800 carbon-fibre sandwich layups with aluminium honeycomb cores and local front/side reinforcements; sized balanced filament-wound T1100 tank laminates for hoop and longitudinal pressure loads.
  • Planned hand layup, vacuum bagging and autoclave curing for 20 low-volume units against compression moulding for 20,000 higher-volume units; developed lid fastening, saddle-clamp and component-mounting concepts.
  • Built an LS-DYNA explicit impact model with orthotropic composite and honeycomb materials, shell/solid meshes and contact definitions; compared front and side baseline impacts from a 1,300 kg impactor at 13.86 m/s (about 124 kJ).
  • Screened Rohacell foam, aluminium honeycomb, carbon-fibre tubes, cones and a stepped carbon-fibre/honeycomb attenuator using impactor energy transfer and front-panel displacement. The 2 kg stepped concept had the lowest peak displacement in the comparison: about 11 mm, versus a 5 mm design target.
  • Compared manufacturing cost and environmental footprints for both production scales, identifying tank production as a major cost and material-impact driver; documented crash-model limitations including coarse envelope meshing and no mesh-convergence or physical validation study.

Postgraduate NVH portfolio — Oxford Brookes University

Advanced Vehicle Dynamics portfolio — Oxford Brookes University

Battery management, cell balancing and charger validation

2025

Electric Vehicles coursework — Oxford Brookes University

  • Designed a Multisim battery-management logic circuit with differential/comparator op-amps, MOSFET switching, overcurrent protection and 3 V undercharge / 4 V overcharge thresholds for the modelled cells.
  • Simulated bypass of an early-full cell during charging and isolation of an undercharged cell during discharge; separately modelled active charge transfer from a higher-voltage cell to a lower-voltage cell.
  • Designed an op-amp/PNP constant-current charger targeting approximately 15 mA at 12 V, with a resistor sweep across 47–2,000 Ω.
  • Built the charger on a breadboard and compared current/voltage curves with Multisim results, observing close agreement in the tested range and current falloff after the constant-current region.
  • Recorded limitations: capacitor substitutes for battery cells, separate management and balancing circuits, undercharge leakage, and no complete CCCV charging phase.
